assessment_membership.source: C2-b authoring declaration (2026-09-26): this target is placed in the V1 placement bank's pragmatic-formula set by this cut's authoring review. The declaration is made here — no authoring fixture and no external assessment export in this repository places this target, so the membership is this review's own and is recorded as such.

texts.text: An apology offered before cutting into what someone else is saying, normally followed by the reason for the interruption.

The formula is sorry to + base verb, and the base verb is what marks the apology as being made while the act is happening: sorry to interrupt, sorry to bother you, sorry to stop you. A but and the reason usually follow (sorry to interrupt, but I have a quick question). The related form sorry for + -ing looks back at an act that is already done or is being done (sorry for interrupting you earlier); both are current English, and the choice between them is about the timing of the apology, not about correctness.

The two shapes are what learners mix: sorry to + base verb, sorry for + -ing. Mixing them produces sorry to interrupting and sorry for interrupt, and neither is English. The one-sentence rule is that to takes the plain verb and for takes the -ing form, so the form after the preposition decides the shape of the verb.

sorry to interrupt = the apology made as the interruption happens (this target). sorry for interrupting = the apology for the act, normally once it is done. sorry that + clause apologises for a fact rather than for an act (sorry that I am late). Excuse me and may I just say are other ways into an interruption with their own register.
抱歉打断一下（在插话之前先道歉，再接上自己要说的事）

pedagogical_profile.rationale: Bands are the C2-b authoring judgement (V1 carries no calibration data): the formula is easy to recognise and frequent wherever several people talk, so receptive value is HIGH and receptive difficulty LOW; productive value is MEDIUM because a learner can interrupt with excuse me instead, and productive difficulty is MEDIUM because the to + base verb and for + -ing split is the shape production has to choose between. RESOURCE_PRACTICE follows the entity's own declared learning_intent ESTABLISH. Revisit when Calibration100 response data exists.

pack_overlays.rationale: The formula belongs to the general fluency pack's politeness set, so it carries substantial weight there; the shortfall records that it is situational rather than general and that the pack's own review has not placed it.
Interrupting a meeting politely is the workplace pack's own subject matter (sorry to interrupt, but the client is on the line), so it carries full weight in that pack.

example_policy.policy: Present at most two examples per attempt, whole sentences only: the canonical sentence first; a SUPPORTING or CONTRAST sentence only after the learner has attempted the canonical form twice without producing it. When the for + -ing variant is shown at all, show it as a CONTRAST with its own timing note, never as a model of the same moment of speaking.

typical_errors.error_pattern: sorry to + verb in -ing form (sorry to interrupting)
typical_errors.explanation: The two apologies are blended: the to of sorry to is kept but the -ing that belongs with sorry for is attached to the verb. to takes the plain verb here, so the shape has to be chosen once rather than mixed.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when to follows sorry and an -ing form follows to.

typical_errors.error_pattern: sorry for + base verb (sorry for interrupt)
typical_errors.explanation: for is a preposition and takes an -ing complement, so a bare verb after it is not a form English has. The learner has the right two words and the wrong verb shape after the second one.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when for follows sorry and a base verb follows for, with no -ing form.

detection_policy.policy: Fires only on the learner's own produced English text, and only on a visible surface form: the words sorry, to or for, and the shape of the verb that follows. No model judgement and no confidence score participates (PRODUCT_CONTRACT §8.1: V1 does not treat a model's self-reported high confidence as an R4 certification). Each rule below states the positive direction it must match; the fixture with the same ordinal states a case the rule must NOT match, so every rule ships with a testable boundary. expected values are NO_MATCH (the shape is absent) and NO_MATCH_BOUNDARY (sorry goes with a that-clause or stands alone as an apology for a fact or a state, so the interruption formula is not in use).

detection_rules.rule: ING_AFTER_TO: match when sorry to is followed by an -ing form, because to in this apology takes the base verb.
BASE_VERB_AFTER_FOR: match when sorry for is followed by a base verb, because for is a preposition and takes an -ing complement.

ACCEPTED_REALIZATIONS: do not match when sorry to takes a base verb (sorry to interrupt, sorry to bother you) or when sorry for takes an -ing form (sorry for interrupting, sorry for being late): both are current English and each is the accepted realization of its own shape.

APOLOGY_FOR_A_FACT_OR_STATE: do not match when sorry stands with a that-clause (sorry that I am late) or with a noun phrase naming a state (sorry about the noise), because the interruption formula is not in use there.
